District leans Democratic by eight points with a favorable environment for incumbents

model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: Harder has out-raised McBride roughly sixty to one, the district's eight-point Democratic lean is reinforced by incumbency and the money gap, and markets on both major platforms put his odds at 95 percent or better. With no polls suggesting otherwise, a Safe Democratic rating is warranted.
model.watch: Because no polling exists in the district, a late scandal or an unusually strong Republican national wave is the main thing that could tighten the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Josh Harder, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a district that leans Democratic by eight points. He has raised more than $4.4 million and holds $4.7 million on hand, while Republican John McBride has raised about $76,000 with under $8,000 remaining. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Harder's chances between 95 and 97 percent.

The fundamentals point the same direction: the district lean, incumbency, the money gap, and a favorable environment add up to an expected margin near twenty points. McBride would need an outside force far beyond anything in the record to close that distance. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, with the main caveat being the absence of direct polling to confirm the fundamentals.
